---
title: Map domain error classes onto a closed error code union
id: ADR-014
status: accepted
owners: [platform-team]
last_updated: 2026-02-19
related: [REQ-138, ADR-003, ADR-004, ADR-009, ADR-012]
---

# ADR-014 — Map domain error classes onto a closed error code union

## Status

Accepted, and treated as the mandatory error-handling contract for every
Server Action and Route Handler in the product — no mutation path is exempt.

## Context

Before this ADR, in December 2025 and January 2026, error handling in
Server Actions was ad hoc: some caught specific error classes and returned a
tailored message, some let errors propagate raw (which, in the App Router,
meant a generic Next.js error boundary rendering "something went wrong" with
no field-level detail), and none agreed on an HTTP-status-equivalent code the
client could branch on. This became a concrete product problem once REQ-138
was written — "exceeding a quota produces `plan_limit_exceeded`, not a
crash" — because at the time there was no `plan_limit_exceeded` concept
anywhere in the code; a quota breach was just a thrown `Error` with a plain
string message, indistinguishable, from the client's point of view, from any
other unexpected failure.

By that point the domain layer already had several purpose-built error
classes serving different concerns — `PermissionDeniedError` from ADR-003,
`TenantScopeError` from ADR-006, `AlreadyArchivedError` from ADR-004, plus
`FeatureDisabledError` (ADR-012) and `InvalidSlugError` (slug validation) —
each thrown from its own module, each carrying different, useful metadata
(`PermissionDeniedError` carries the denied `action` and the `reason` code
from `explain()`; `TenantScopeError` carries the expected and actual
`orgId`). The team needed a single place that turned any of these, plus
Zod's own `ZodError` from ADR-009, into one closed, predictable client-facing
shape, without each Server Action re-implementing that translation.

## Decision

`src/lib/errors.ts` defines `HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE`, a
`Readonly<Record<ErrorCode, number>>` covering exactly nine codes:
`unauthorized` (401), `forbidden` (403), `not_found` (404),
`validation_failed` (422), `conflict` (409), `rate_limited` (429),
`plan_limit_exceeded` (402), `tenant_scope_violation` (403), and
`internal_error` (500). This is a closed union — `ErrorCode` in
`src/types/api.ts` — and every domain error the service layer is permitted to
throw maps onto exactly one of these codes, never a raw string.

`isDomainError(error)` recognizes the known, deliberately-thrown classes:
`PermissionDeniedError`, `TenantScopeError`, `FeatureDisabledError`,
`AlreadyArchivedError`, `InvalidSlugError`, and `ZodError` — the module's own
documentation states these are the error classes "this module knows how to
translate faithfully," implying, correctly, that anything else is treated as
an unexpected internal failure. `toAppError(error)` is the actual mapping
function: `ZodError` becomes `validation_failed` with `fieldErrorsFromZod()`
populating per-field messages; `PermissionDeniedError` becomes `forbidden`
with `meta` carrying the denied action, resource kind, and `explain()`
reason code (`denied_cross_tenant`, `denied_by_role`, and so on) so a client
that wants to log or display *why* access was denied can, without
re-deriving it; `TenantScopeError` becomes `tenant_scope_violation` with the
expected and actual org ids in `meta`; `FeatureDisabledError` becomes
`forbidden` with the flag key; `AlreadyArchivedError` becomes `conflict` with
the entity and id; `InvalidSlugError` becomes `validation_failed` with a
`slug` field error. Anything not recognized by `isDomainError()` falls
through to `internal_error`, with the raw `Error.message` surfaced only if
the thrown value actually was an `Error` instance, otherwise a fixed generic
string — deliberately not leaking arbitrary thrown values (a string, an
object, whatever a third-party dependency might throw) to the client
verbatim.

`toActionResult(error)` wraps `toAppError()`'s output into the failure half of
the `ActionResult<T>` discriminated union every Server Action returns
(`{ ok: false, error, submittedAt }`), which is what `withAction()`
(`src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts`, ADR-013) calls in its catch block, so an
individual Server Action's own code never needs a try/catch around its
service call at all — the wrapper is where errors become results.

## Consequences

**What this buys the team.** REQ-138 is now trivially true by construction:
a billing quota check throws a plain `Error` today (there is no
`PlanLimitExceededError` class yet — a known gap, see below), but every
*other* domain concern already has a precise code, and the pattern this ADR
establishes is exactly what a future `PlanLimitExceededError` would slot
into. Every client-facing error the product produces now has a stable,
finite vocabulary of nine codes, which makes client-side error handling
(toast messages, inline field errors, redirect-to-login on `unauthorized`)
a matter of switching on `code`, not on parsing message strings. The `meta`
payloads turned into a real debugging and support tool — Jan Novak's SRE
runbooks reference `TenantScopeError`'s `meta.expectedOrgId` /
`meta.actualOrgId` fields directly when triaging a reported cross-tenant
access attempt, because the error itself carries the two org ids that
matter rather than requiring a log correlation exercise.

**What it costs, and what remains a gap.** The mapping function has to be
extended every time a new domain error class is introduced, and forgetting
to do so means the new error class falls through to `internal_error` — safe
in the sense that it does not leak detail, but unhelpful in the sense that a
genuinely expected, recoverable condition (a plan-limit breach, today) gets
treated identically to a genuine bug. This is the concrete, currently-live
gap: `wouldExceedLimit()` (ADR-010) is called by billing-adjacent code, but
nothing yet throws a dedicated `PlanLimitExceededError` that `toAppError()`
recognizes — REQ-139's requirement that quota breaches emit
`billing.limit_exceeded` is satisfied at the event-bus level (ADR-005), but
the *error* a blocked mutation returns to the client today is a generic
`Error`, mapped to `internal_error`, not the `plan_limit_exceeded` code this
ADR's own status table already reserves for it. The platform team has this
tracked as follow-up work, not disputed as a design question — the code and
the HTTP status already exist in `HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE`, waiting for the
corresponding error class.

## Alternatives considered

**Let each Server Action catch and translate errors itself.** This is what
the codebase had before, and it produced exactly the inconsistency (some
actions detailed, some generic, none agreeing on codes) that motivated this
ADR. Rejected for the same "one place to look, one place to change" reasoning
behind ADR-003 and ADR-010.

**An open-ended error code space** (any string the throwing code chooses,
rather than a closed nine-value union). Rejected because it removes the
guarantee that `HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE` is exhaustive — a client branching on
`error.code` would have no compile-time assurance it had handled every
possible value, and a new ad hoc code introduced by one Server Action could
silently have no corresponding HTTP status mapping anywhere.

**Encode the error code inside the HTTP status alone**, without a separate
`ErrorCode` string, relying on the numeric status for client branching.
Rejected because two of the nine codes intentionally share an HTTP status
(`forbidden` and `tenant_scope_violation` are both 403) but mean genuinely
different things to the client — a tenant-scope violation should probably
never be retried or reported the same way a permission denial is, even
though both are "403" at the transport level.

## References

- REQ-138 (exceeding a quota produces `plan_limit_exceeded`, not a crash —
  the currently-incomplete case this ADR documents honestly)
- ADR-003 (`PermissionDeniedError`, mapped here to `forbidden`), ADR-004
  (`AlreadyArchivedError`, mapped here to `conflict`), ADR-009 (`ZodError`,
  mapped here to `validation_failed`), ADR-012 (`FeatureDisabledError`,
  mapped here to `forbidden`)
- Code: `src/lib/errors.ts` (`HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE`, `isDomainError`,
  `toAppError`, `fieldErrorsFromZod`, `toActionResult`), `src/types/api.ts`
  (`ErrorCode`, `ActionResult`, `AppErrorShape`),
  `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts`

1	---
2	title: Billing actions
3	id: API-ACTIONS-BILLING
4	status: approved
5	owners: [r.saito]
6	last_updated: 2026-05-29
7	related: [REQ-130, REQ-131, REQ-138, REQ-141, DES-135, DES-136, DES-248, ADR-010]
8	---
9	
10	# Billing actions
11	
12	Three files under src/actions/billing/: cancel a subscription, change plan, update seats.
13	All three gate on the single `org:manage_billing` permission, which sits at owner rank in
14	`ROLE_MATRIX` — the highest floor any action in the corpus requires, shared only with
15	`org:delete`. The interesting behavior in this group is not the permission check, which is
16	identical and trivial across all three; it is how each one decides whether a requested
17	change is safe against the organization's *current* usage before letting it through.
18	
19	## `changePlanAction`
20	
21	- **File:** `src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts`
22	- **Input schema:** `changePlanSchema` (`src/schemas/billing.ts`) — `ChangePlanInput`
23	- **Returns:** `ActionResult<Subscription>`
24	- **Permission:** `org:manage_billing` (minimum role owner; see DES-043)
25	- **Feature flag:** none
26	- **Rate limit bucket:** none
27	- **Plan limit:** `seats`, `projects`, `storageMb` — checked against the *target* plan
28	- **Events emitted:** `billing.plan_changed` (via `changePlan()`)
29	- **Cache tags revalidated:** `orgTag(input.orgId)`, `CACHE_PROFILES.hours`
30	- **Errors:** `validation_failed`, `forbidden`, `plan_limit_exceeded`, `internal_error`
31	- **Satisfies:** REQ-131, REQ-140, REQ-141
32	- **Design:** DES-136, DES-248
33	
34	### Input fields
35	
36	| field | type | required | notes |
37	|---|---|---|---|
38	| `orgId` | branded `OrgId` | yes | |
39	| `plan` | `"free" \| "starter" \| "growth" \| "enterprise"` | yes | `planIdSchema` |
40	| `interval` | `"monthly" \| "annual"` | no, default `"monthly"` | |
41	
42	### Behaviour
43	
44	After the `org:manage_billing` check, `assertPlanFitsCurrentUsage()` — a private helper in
45	this file — reads live usage via `getUsage()` and compares three dimensions (`seats`,
46	`projects`, `storageMb`) against the *target* plan's limits using
47	`wouldExceedLimit(input.plan, resource, used, 0)`, with a requested delta of **zero**. The
48	comment in the source explains the zero deliberately: "we are not consuming anything, only
49	asking whether what is already in use still fits." This is DES-136 and DES-248: a plan
50	change is checked against every relevant usage dimension before the plan row changes, using
51	the target plan's limits, not the current plan's — so an org on `growth` with 40 seats that
52	tries to move to `starter` (10 seats) is refused with `PlanLimitError("seats", 10, 40)`
53	before the subscription row is touched at all. This is REQ-141: downgrades are refused while
54	usage exceeds the target plan. The check loops all three resources and throws on the first
55	one that would not fit, using that resource's own `used`/`limit` pair in the error, so an org
56	failing on `projects` rather than `seats` gets an error that names `projects` specifically
57	rather than a generic "this plan doesn't fit" message.
58	
59	Notice what is *not* checked: `issuesPerProject`, `apiRequestsPerHour`, and `webhooks` are
60	plan-limited resources (per `PlanLimits` in `src/config/plan-limits.ts`) that this action
61	does not verify against the target plan. A downgrade from `growth` to `starter` that would
62	leave an org with more webhook endpoints than `starter`'s ceiling of 2 allows is not blocked
63	by this action — the endpoints simply become over-limit going forward, silently, unless a
64	separate cron job or read-time check catches it. This is a gap in the downgrade guard's
65	coverage worth knowing rather than assuming is comprehensive.
66	
67	## `updateSeatsAction`
68	
69	- **File:** `src/actions/billing/update-seats.ts`
70	- **Input schema:** `updateSeatsSchema` (`src/schemas/billing.ts`) — `UpdateSeatsInput`
71	- **Returns:** `ActionResult<Subscription>`
72	- **Permission:** `org:manage_billing` (minimum role owner; see DES-043)
73	- **Feature flag:** none
74	- **Rate limit bucket:** none
75	- **Plan limit:** `seats`, bounded on both sides
76	- **Events emitted:** none directly documented at the action layer beyond what
77	  `updateSeats()` itself emits
78	- **Cache tags revalidated:** `orgTag(input.orgId)`, `CACHE_PROFILES.hours`
79	- **Errors:** `validation_failed`, `forbidden`, `plan_limit_exceeded`, `internal_error`
80	- **Satisfies:** REQ-133
81	- **Design:** DES-249
82	
83	### Input fields
84	
85	| field | type | required | notes |
86	|---|---|---|---|
87	| `orgId` | branded `OrgId` | yes | |
88	| `seats` | integer, 1-10000 | yes | `updateSeatsSchema` |
89	
90	### Behaviour
91	
92	DES-249: **`update-seats` is bounded in both directions**, unlike a quota check that only
93	guards against exceeding a ceiling. After reading `getOrganizationSummary()` for
94	`summary.usage.seatsUsed` and `getPlanLimits(summary.organization.plan)` for the current
95	plan's `seats` ceiling, the action checks two separate conditions: `input.seats >
96	limits.seats` throws `PlanLimitError("seats", limits.seats, input.seats)` (you cannot raise
97	seats above the plan's own maximum — an org on `starter`, ceiling 10, cannot set 15 seats
98	without first changing plan), and `input.seats < summary.usage.seatsUsed` throws
99	`PlanLimitError("seats", input.seats, summary.usage.seatsUsed)` (you cannot lower seats below
100	the count of members actually occupying them). The two checks use the `PlanLimitError`
101	constructor's `limit`/`used` positions differently in each direction — the first reports the
102	plan ceiling as the limit, the second reports the *requested* seat count as the limit and
103	current usage as what's used — which is worth noticing if you are writing a client-side
104	error renderer that assumes `limit` always means "the plan's number": here it sometimes means
105	"the number you just tried to set."
106	
107	## `cancelSubscriptionAction`
108	
109	- **File:** `src/actions/billing/cancel-subscription.ts`
110	- **Input schema:** `cancelSubscriptionSchema` (`src/schemas/billing.ts`) —
111	  `CancelSubscriptionInput`
112	- **Returns:** `ActionResult<Subscription>`
113	- **Permission:** `org:manage_billing` (minimum role owner; see DES-043)
114	- **Feature flag:** none
115	- **Rate limit bucket:** none
116	- **Plan limit:** none — cancellation is never blocked by a quota check
117	- **Events emitted:** none documented in the action file beyond what
118	  `cancelSubscription()` itself emits
119	- **Cache tags revalidated:** `orgTag(input.orgId)`, `CACHE_PROFILES.hours`
120	- **Errors:** `validation_failed`, `forbidden`, `internal_error`
121	- **Satisfies:** REQ-130
122	- **Design:** none of the DES-1xx catalogue documents this action's own file in detail
123	  beyond what is captured here — see `design/service-billing-and-usage.md` for the
124	  service-layer cancellation semantics
125	
126	### Input fields
127	
128	| field | type | required | notes |
129	|---|---|---|---|
130	| `orgId` | branded `OrgId` | yes | |
131	| `reason` | string, max 500 | no | free-text, stored for support/analytics purposes |
132	| `cancelImmediately` | boolean | no, default `false` | `false` cancels at period end |
133	
134	### Behaviour
135	
136	The source comment for this file is unusually short compared to the rest of the corpus:
137	"only an owner may cancel — `org:manage_billing` sits at owner level in `ROLE_MATRIX`, so
138	the `can()` call below is the whole guard." That is accurate — unlike `change-plan.ts` and
139	`update-seats.ts`, this action performs no usage comparison before calling
140	`cancelSubscription()`; there is nothing to check a cancellation against, since canceling
141	never raises any resource's effective ceiling for the org, only lowers or ends it eventually.
142	The `cancelImmediately` flag is passed straight through to the service, which is responsible
143	for the difference between "stop billing now" and "keep access through the current period,
144	stop at renewal" — the action layer does not distinguish the two beyond forwarding the
145	boolean.
146	
147	## Downgrade guard sequence
148	
149	```mermaid
150	sequenceDiagram
151	    participant Owner as billing settings page
152	    participant Action as changePlanAction
153	    participant Perm as can("org:manage_billing")
154	    participant Usage as getUsage()
155	    participant Limits as getPlanLimits(targetPlan)
156	    participant Svc as BillingService.changePlan()
157	
158	    Owner->>Action: changePlanAction({ orgId, plan: "starter" })
159	    Action->>Perm: can(actor, "org:manage_billing", ...)
160	    alt not owner
161	        Perm-->>Action: false
162	        Action-->>Owner: { ok: false, error: { code: "forbidden" } }
163	    else owner
164	        Perm-->>Action: true
165	        Action->>Usage: getUsage(actor, orgId)
166	        Usage-->>Action: { seatsUsed, projectsUsed, storageMbUsed }
167	        Action->>Limits: getPlanLimits("starter")
168	        loop seats, projects, storageMb
169	            Action->>Action: wouldExceedLimit("starter", resource, used, 0)
170	        end
171	        alt any resource would exceed
172	            Action-->>Owner: { ok: false, error: { code: "plan_limit_exceeded" } }
173	        else all three fit
174	            Action->>Svc: changePlan(actor, input)
175	            Svc-->>Action: Subscription (billing.plan_changed emitted)
176	            Action-->>Owner: { ok: true, data: subscription }
177	        end
178	    end
179	```
180	
181	## The plan ladder these actions enforce against
182	
183	`PLAN_ORDER` (`src/config/plan-limits.ts`) declares four plans, and the seat/project/storage
184	ceilings `changePlanAction` and `updateSeatsAction` compare usage against are:
185	
186	| plan | seats | projects | storageMb | webhooks |
187	|---|---|---|---|---|
188	| `free` | 3 | 2 | 100 | 0 |
189	| `starter` | 10 | 10 | 2000 | 2 |
190	| `growth` | 50 | 100 | 20000 | 10 |
191	| `enterprise` | UNLIMITED | UNLIMITED | 500000 | UNLIMITED |
192	
193	`UNLIMITED` is `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (REQ-137), which is why `wouldExceedLimit` never
194	needs a special case for the enterprise plan — comparing any finite usage number against
195	`Infinity` is always `false`, so the downgrade guard and the seat-bounds check both fall out
196	of the same arithmetic without a conditional branch for "this plan has no ceiling." An owner
197	moving an organization *up* the ladder (say, `starter` to `growth`) never triggers
198	`PlanLimitError` from either action, since every ceiling on the target plan is at least as
199	generous as the current one — the guard logic in this file only ever has teeth on a
200	downgrade.
201	
202	## Why three actions share one permission and no others do
203	
204	`org:manage_billing`'s owner-only floor is shared with exactly one other action in the
205	entire `ROLE_MATRIX`: `org:delete`. The team's reasoning, recorded in
206	`design/permission-model.md`, is that both categories of action can change what the
207	organization *is able to afford* — deleting it outright, or changing what it pays and how
208	many seats it can fill — in ways that an admin, who can already manage members, projects,
209	and flags, should not be able to trigger unilaterally. Every other action documented in this
210	directory sits at admin rank or below; this file is the one place in the whole `actions-*`
211	documentation set where every single action shares the single highest permission floor in
212	the matrix.
213	
214	## What `Subscription` carries back
215	
216	All three actions return `ActionResult<Subscription>`, and the `Subscription` type (not
217	detailed further here — see `design/repository-billing-and-usage.md`) is what the billing
218	settings page renders after each mutation: plan, interval, status
219	(`trialing`/`active`/`past_due`/`canceled`), and the period boundaries. Because
220	`cancelSubscriptionAction` with `cancelImmediately: false` still returns a `Subscription`
221	whose `status` may remain `"active"` until the period actually ends, a client that
222	naively treats "the action succeeded" as "access has already changed" will render an
223	incorrect state — the correct read is the returned subscription's own `status` and period
224	fields, not the mere fact that the action resolved with `ok: true`.
225	
226	## `cancelSubscriptionSchema`'s `reason` field
227	
228	`reason` on `cancelSubscriptionAction`'s input is the only free-text field anywhere in this
229	action group, and it is optional — nothing in the action or the service layer requires a
230	reason to be given, and nothing validates its content beyond the 500-character cap. It exists
231	purely to be stored alongside the cancellation for whoever later reviews churn (support,
232	finance), and this action's own behavior does not branch on its value at all; two
233	cancellations that differ only in `reason` produce identical `Subscription` results and
234	identical cache invalidation. Treat it as an audit annotation, not a parameter the mutation's
235	logic reads.
236	
237	## Relationship to the settings billing page
238	
239	The three actions in this file back the three primary controls on
240	`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/billing/page.tsx` — the plan picker, the seat
241	stepper, and the cancel-subscription control — which itself reads `getPlanLimits` directly
242	(per `design/module-map.md`'s manifest) to render the same ceiling numbers these actions
243	enforce, so the UI's own "seats used: 8 of 10" meter and the error a caller gets back from
244	`updateSeatsAction` are computed from the same source table rather than two independently
245	maintained copies of the plan ladder.
246	
247	## Trials are handled elsewhere
248	
249	None of these three actions mentions trials, and that is deliberate: REQ-142 (trials expire
250	on a schedule and fall back to free) is enforced by `trial-expiry-job` (see
251	`route-handlers.md`'s cron trigger table and `design/background-jobs.md`, DES-068), not by
252	any user-invoked action. `changePlanAction` is available to an org still on `trialing`
253	status just as it is to one on `active`, and choosing a plan while trialing is an ordinary
254	plan change from this action's point of view — DES-207 (an unconditional exit from
255	`trialing`, never a re-entry) is a repository-layer invariant this action relies on without
256	implementing itself.
257	
258	Related: REQ-132, REQ-134, REQ-135, REQ-136, REQ-137, REQ-139, REQ-142, REQ-143, REQ-144,
259	DES-137, DES-138, DES-139, DES-140, DES-141, ADR-010.
260

## `cancelSubscriptionAction`

- **File:** `src/actions/billing/cancel-subscription.ts`
- **Input schema:** `cancelSubscriptionSchema` (`src/schemas/billing.ts`) —
  `CancelSubscriptionInput`
- **Returns:** `ActionResult<Subscription>`
- **Permission:** `org:manage_billing` (minimum role owner; see DES-043)
- **Feature flag:** none
- **Rate limit bucket:** none
- **Plan limit:** none — cancellation is never blocked by a quota check
- **Events emitted:** none documented in the action file beyond what
  `cancelSubscription()` itself emits
- **Cache tags revalidated:** `orgTag(input.orgId)`, `CACHE_PROFILES.hours`
- **Errors:** `validation_failed`, `forbidden`, `internal_error`
- **Satisfies:** REQ-130
- **Design:** none of the DES-1xx catalogue documents this action's own file in detail
  beyond what is captured here — see `design/service-billing-and-usage.md` for the
  service-layer cancellation semantics

### Input fields

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `orgId` | branded `OrgId` | yes | |
| `reason` | string, max 500 | no | free-text, stored for support/analytics purposes |
| `cancelImmediately` | boolean | no, default `false` | `false` cancels at period end |

### Behaviour

The source comment for this file is unusually short compared to the rest of the corpus:
"only an owner may cancel — `org:manage_billing` sits at owner level in `ROLE_MATRIX`, so
the `can()` call below is the whole guard." That is accurate — unlike `change-plan.ts` and
`update-seats.ts`, this action performs no usage comparison before calling
`cancelSubscription()`; there is nothing to check a cancellation against, since canceling
never raises any resource's effective ceiling for the org, only lowers or ends it eventually.
The `cancelImmediately` flag is passed straight through to the service, which is responsible
for the difference between "stop billing now" and "keep access through the current period,
stop at renewal" — the action layer does not distinguish the two beyond forwarding the
boolean.

## Downgrade guard sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Owner as billing settings page
    participant Action as changePlanAction
    participant Perm as can("org:manage_billing")
    participant Usage as getUsage()
    participant Limits as getPlanLimits(targetPlan)
    participant Svc as BillingService.changePlan()

    Owner->>Action: changePlanAction({ orgId, plan: "starter" })
    Action->>Perm: can(actor, "org:manage_billing", ...)
    alt not owner
        Perm-->>Action: false
        Action-->>Owner: { ok: false, error: { code: "forbidden" } }
    else owner
        Perm-->>Action: true
        Action->>Usage: getUsage(actor, orgId)
        Usage-->>Action: { seatsUsed, projectsUsed, storageMbUsed }
        Action->>Limits: getPlanLimits("starter")
        loop seats, projects, storageMb
            Action->>Action: wouldExceedLimit("starter", resource, used, 0)
        end
        alt any resource would exceed
            Action-->>Owner: { ok: false, error: { code: "plan_limit_exceeded" } }
        else all three fit
            Action->>Svc: changePlan(actor, input)
            Svc-->>Action: Subscription (billing.plan_changed emitted)
            Action-->>Owner: { ok: true, data: subscription }
        end
    end
```

## The plan ladder these actions enforce against

`PLAN_ORDER` (`src/config/plan-limits.ts`) declares four plans, and the seat/project/storage
ceilings `changePlanAction` and `updateSeatsAction` compare usage against are:

| plan | seats | projects | storageMb | webhooks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `free` | 3 | 2 | 100 | 0 |
| `starter` | 10 | 10 | 2000 | 2 |
| `growth` | 50 | 100 | 20000 | 10 |
| `enterprise` | UNLIMITED | UNLIMITED | 500000 | UNLIMITED |

`UNLIMITED` is `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (REQ-137), which is why `wouldExceedLimit` never
needs a special case for the enterprise plan — comparing any finite usage number against
`Infinity` is always `false`, so the downgrade guard and the seat-bounds check both fall out
of the same arithmetic without a conditional branch for "this plan has no ceiling." An owner
moving an organization *up* the ladder (say, `starter` to `growth`) never triggers
`PlanLimitError` from either action, since every ceiling on the target plan is at least as
generous as the current one — the guard logic in this file only ever has teeth on a
downgrade.

## Why three actions share one permission and no others do

`org:manage_billing`'s owner-only floor is shared with exactly one other action in the
entire `ROLE_MATRIX`: `org:delete`. The team's reasoning, recorded in
`design/permission-model.md`, is that both categories of action can change what the
organization *is able to afford* — deleting it outright, or changing what it pays and how
many seats it can fill — in ways that an admin, who can already manage members, projects,
and flags, should not be able to trigger unilaterally. Every other action documented in this
directory sits at admin rank or below; this file is the one place in the whole `actions-*`
documentation set where every single action shares the single highest permission floor in
the matrix.

## What `Subscription` carries back

All three actions return `ActionResult<Subscription>`, and the `Subscription` type (not
detailed further here — see `design/repository-billing-and-usage.md`) is what the billing
settings page renders after each mutation: plan, interval, status
(`trialing`/`active`/`past_due`/`canceled`), and the period boundaries. Because
`cancelSubscriptionAction` with `cancelImmediately: false` still returns a `Subscription`
whose `status` may remain `"active"` until the period actually ends, a client that
naively treats "the action succeeded" as "access has already changed" will render an
incorrect state — the correct read is the returned subscription's own `status` and period
fields, not the mere fact that the action resolved with `ok: true`.

## `cancelSubscriptionSchema`'s `reason` field

`reason` on `cancelSubscriptionAction`'s input is the only free-text field anywhere in this
action group, and it is optional — nothing in the action or the service layer requires a
reason to be given, and nothing validates its content beyond the 500-character cap. It exists
purely to be stored alongside the cancellation for whoever later reviews churn (support,
finance), and this action's own behavior does not branch on its value at all; two
cancellations that differ only in `reason` produce identical `Subscription` results and
identical cache invalidation. Treat it as an audit annotation, not a parameter the mutation's
logic reads.

## Relationship to the settings billing page

The three actions in this file back the three primary controls on
`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/billing/page.tsx` — the plan picker, the seat
stepper, and the cancel-subscription control — which itself reads `getPlanLimits` directly
(per `design/module-map.md`'s manifest) to render the same ceiling numbers these actions
enforce, so the UI's own "seats used: 8 of 10" meter and the error a caller gets back from
`updateSeatsAction` are computed from the same source table rather than two independently
maintained copies of the plan ladder.

## Trials are handled elsewhere

None of these three actions mentions trials, and that is deliberate: REQ-142 (trials expire
on a schedule and fall back to free) is enforced by `trial-expiry-job` (see
`route-handlers.md`'s cron trigger table and `design/background-jobs.md`, DES-068), not by
any user-invoked action. `changePlanAction` is available to an org still on `trialing`
status just as it is to one on `active`, and choosing a plan while trialing is an ordinary
plan change from this action's point of view — DES-207 (an unconditional exit from
`trialing`, never a re-entry) is a repository-layer invariant this action relies on without
implementing itself.

Related: REQ-132, REQ-134, REQ-135, REQ-136, REQ-137, REQ-139, REQ-142, REQ-143, REQ-144,
DES-137, DES-138, DES-139, DES-140, DES-141, ADR-010.

## Decision

`src/config/plan-limits.ts` declares `PlanLimits` as a single interface —
`plan`, `seats`, `projects`, `issuesPerProject`, `storageMb`,
`apiRequestsPerHour`, `webhooks`, `retentionDays`, `includedFlags`,
`priceCentsPerSeatMonthly` — and `PLAN_LIMITS` as a `Readonly<Record<PlanId,
PlanLimits>>` covering all four plans completely: free (3 seats, 2 projects,
100 issues/project, 100 MB storage, 100 API req/hr, 0 webhooks, 30-day
retention, free price), starter (10/10/1,000/2,000/1,000/2/90 days/$9.00 per
seat), growth (50/100/10,000/20,000/10,000/10/365 days/$19.00 per seat), and
enterprise (unlimited seats, projects, and issues per project, 500,000 MB
storage, 100,000 API req/hr, unlimited webhooks, 2,555-day retention,
$39.00 per seat). `UNLIMITED` is declared once as `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`
and used everywhere a quota has no ceiling — REQ-137 requires unlimited be
represented this way specifically so downstream arithmetic (`used + requested
> limit`) behaves correctly without a special-cased "is this unlimited"
branch scattered through call sites.

Every consumer reads through one of four functions, never the `PLAN_LIMITS`

---
title: Notes — plan ladder pricing
id: OPS-NOTES-2026-02-10
status: approved
owners: [r.saito]
last_updated: 2026-02-10
related: [ADR-010, REQ-131, REQ-132]
---

**Date:** 2026-02-10
**Attendees:** r.saito (chair), a.whitfield, d.okafor, m.lindqvist

## Agenda

1. Finalize the four-plan ladder's numeric limits ahead of `PLAN_LIMITS` being frozen in
   code.
2. Decide the `enterprise` plan's price and whether any dimension should stay
   unlimited versus a large finite number.
3. Discuss the `UNLIMITED` representation and whether `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` is
   actually safe to use in downstream arithmetic.

## Discussion

Rin presented the draft ladder: `free` (3 seats, 2 projects, 100 issues per project, 100
MB storage, 100 API requests/hour, 0 webhooks, 30-day retention, $0), `starter` (10/10/
1000/2000/1000/2/90/$900 per seat monthly), `growth` (50/100/10000/20000/10000/10/365/
$1900), and `enterprise` (unlimited seats, projects, and issues per project, 500000 MB
storage, 100000 API requests/hour, unlimited webhooks, 2555-day retention, $3900).

Ada pushed back on `enterprise` webhooks being unlimited rather than a large finite
number, worried that "unlimited webhooks" as a literal product claim could be abused by
a single enterprise customer registering thousands of endpoints and degrading the shared
webhook delivery pipeline for everyone — a concern that, in hindsight after
`postmortem-2026-04-17-webhook-backlog.md`, turned out to be prescient about
throughput risk generally, even though that incident was triggered by event volume
rather than endpoint count specifically. The group discussed capping enterprise
webhooks at a large finite number like 500 instead. Deji argued that from an engineering
standpoint, "unlimited" and "500" require the same code — a numeric comparison against
`getPlanLimits(plan).webhooks` either way — so the decision was really a product and
sales question, not a technical one. Ada ultimately kept `enterprise` webhooks unlimited

1	---
2	title: Server Action wrapper, errors and permission resources
3	id: DES-ACTION-CORE
4	status: approved
5	owners: [platform-team, d.okafor]
6	last_updated: 2026-06-12
7	related: [REQ-200, REQ-210, REQ-211, ADR-001, ADR-003, ADR-009, ADR-014, DES-070, DES-100]
8	---
9	
10	## Purpose
11	
12	This document covers the three files under src/actions/_lib/: `with-action.ts`,
13	`action-errors.ts` and `permission-resources.ts`. Every Server Action in the corpus except
14	five deliberately documented exceptions funnels through `withAction()`. These three files
15	are the load-bearing plumbing of the entire mutation surface — the four responsibilities
16	the common brief lists for every mutation ("validate, authenticate, translate errors,
17	revalidate") are implemented exactly once, here, rather than being re-implemented by each
18	of the thirty-nine action files.
19	
20	`with-action.ts`'s own header comment states this concentration of responsibility
21	explicitly: "Owner D. Every mutation in `src/actions/**` funnels through here so the four
22	things each one must do — validate, authenticate, translate errors, revalidate — happen in
23	exactly one place." That sentence is the design thesis of the whole action layer, and this
24	document is where it gets unpacked function by function.
25	
26	## Public surface
27	
28	| function | signature | tables touched | pagination | notes |
29	|---|---|---|---|---|
30	| `withAction` | `<TSchema, TData>(schema, handler, options?) => (raw) => Promise<ActionResult<TData>>` | none directly | — | the wrapper itself |
31	| `resolveActorFor` (private) | `(input, fromInput) => Promise<Actor>` | none directly | — | orgSlug/orgId-from-input, else session |
32	| `stamp` (private) | `<T>(result) => ActionResult<T>` | none | — | attaches `submittedAt` |
33	| `UnauthorizedActionError` | class, `code: "unauthorized"` | — | — | no session, or session with no active org |
34	| `ForbiddenActionError` | class, `code: "forbidden"`, carries `action: PermissionAction` | — | — | `can()` returned false |
35	| `PlanLimitError` | class, `code: "plan_limit_exceeded"`, carries `resource`, `limit`, `used` | — | — | a `LimitedResource` quota would be breached |
36	| `RateLimitedError` | class, `code: "rate_limited"`, carries `bucketKey`, `resetAt` | — | — | `consumeRateLimit` refused |
37	| `FeatureUnavailableError` | class, `code: "forbidden"`, carries `flag` | — | — | a gating flag is off |
38	| `ActionNotFoundError` | class, `code: "not_found"`, carries `what` | — | — | row not found inside the actor's tenant |
39	| `PENDING_ISSUE_ID` / `PENDING_PROJECT_ID` / `PENDING_COMMENT_ID` / `PENDING_MEMBER_ID` | branded empty strings | — | — | create-time `can()` placeholders |
40	| `ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID` | branded empty string | — | — | rate-limit bucket owner pre-session |
41	
42	### DES-220 — `withAction` is the single funnel for validate, authenticate, translate, revalidate
43	
44	- **Satisfies:** REQ-200, REQ-211
45	- **Decided in:** ADR-001, ADR-009
46	- **Code:** `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts` — `withAction`
47	
48	`withAction(schema, handler, options)` returns a closure — `runAction(raw)` — that a given
49	action file exports directly (or, more often, wraps in a one-line named export function so
50	the client-facing name matches the file, e.g. `archiveIssueAction`). Inside `runAction`,
51	the sequence is fixed: `schema.safeParse(raw)` first, returning a stamped failure
52	`ActionResult` immediately on a validation miss without ever calling the handler; then
53	`resolveActorFor()` to get an `Actor`; then the handler itself, wrapped in a `try/catch`
54	that routes every thrown error — domain errors from the service layer, the action-layer
55	error classes from `action-errors.ts`, or anything else — through `toActionResult()` (in
56	`src/lib/errors.ts`, described in the repository documents' cross-references as
57	ADR-014's error-code mapping). On success, `options.revalidate` tags are passed to
58	`revalidateTagged()` with `options.cacheProfile ?? CACHE_PROFILES.minutes` as the
59	cache-life profile Next 16 requires as `revalidateTag`'s second argument. This ordering —
60	validate before authenticate, authenticate before handle, handle before revalidate — is
61	uniform across all thirty-four actions that use `withAction`, which is what lets ADR-009's
62	shared-schema design (the same Zod schema validating both a client form and the action
63	input) actually hold: the schema is always the first gate, never bypassed by a handler that
64	might otherwise be tempted to read a raw field before validation completes.
65	
66	### DES-221 — Actor resolution prefers the payload's own org identity over the session default
67	
68	- **Satisfies:** REQ-210, REQ-211
69	- **Decided in:** ADR-001, ADR-006
70	- **Code:** `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts` — `resolveActorFor`, `ActionOptions.requireOrg`
71	
72	`resolveActorFor(input, fromInput)` checks, when `fromInput` is true (the default, since
73	`ActionOptions.requireOrg` defaults to `true` when not explicitly set to `false`), whether
74	the already-Zod-parsed input object carries a non-empty `orgSlug` string or `orgId` string
75	field. If `orgSlug` is present it calls `getActor(orgSlug)`; if only `orgId` is present it
76	calls `requireActorFor(orgId as OrgId)`. Only when neither is present — or when
77	`options.requireOrg === false`, the path `updateProfileAction` uses — does it fall back to
78	`getSessionPrincipal()` and resolve against `principal.activeOrgId`, throwing
79	`UnauthorizedActionError` if there is no session or no active org. The doc comment on the
80	function explains the split in practical terms: "`getActor(orgSlug)` is the primary path
81	because most mutations are dispatched from a `[orgSlug]` route; actions whose payload
82	carries the branded `orgId` instead resolve through `requireActorFor()`." This preference
83	for the payload's own org identity over whatever happens to be the session's active org is
84	what makes it possible for a single browser session to have two tabs open on two different
85	organizations and mutate the correct one in each — the active-org fallback exists only for
86	the minority of actions, like `updateProfileAction`, that genuinely have no org-bearing
87	field in their payload to resolve against.
88	
89	### DES-222 — Action-layer error classes mirror service-layer domain errors under one closed `ErrorCode` union
90	
91	- **Satisfies:** REQ-138, REQ-193
92	- **Decided in:** ADR-014
93	- **Code:** `src/actions/_lib/action-errors.ts`
94	
95	`action-errors.ts`'s header comment is explicit that these six classes exist at this layer
96	specifically: "these live in src/actions/_lib because only the action layer produces
97	them — services throw their own domain errors, and repositories throw none." Each class
98	carries a `readonly code` matching one of the nine `ErrorCode` values `HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE`
99	in `src/lib/errors.ts` maps to an HTTP status: `UnauthorizedActionError` →
100	`"unauthorized"` (401), `ForbiddenActionError` → `"forbidden"` (403, also shared with
101	`FeatureUnavailableError`), `PlanLimitError` → `"plan_limit_exceeded"` (402),
102	`RateLimitedError` → `"rate_limited"` (429), `ActionNotFoundError` → `"not_found"` (404).
103	This mirrors, rather than duplicates, the convention `PermissionDeniedError` and
104	`TenantScopeError` already establish at the service layer — both layers independently throw
105	typed errors that `toAppError()` translates by `instanceof` check, and `isDomainError()` in
106	`src/lib/errors.ts` recognizes the service-layer set but not this action-layer set by name,
107	because `toActionResult`'s catch-all branch (returning `{ code: "internal_error", ... }`)
108	is only reached for errors *neither* layer recognizes — the action-layer classes are
109	recognized through their own `readonly code` field being read directly in some call sites
110	and through structural equivalence with the service-layer mapping pattern in others. The
111	practical effect for a form author: whichever layer detects the problem first, the shape of
112	what reaches the browser is identical.
113	
114	### DES-223 — `stamp()` attaches `submittedAt` so `useActionState` can distinguish two results
115	
116	- **Satisfies:** REQ-200
117	- **Decided in:** ADR-001
118	- **Code:** `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts` — `stamp`
119	
120	`stamp<T>(result)` is a tiny function — it takes an `ActionResult<T>` that is either `{ ok:
121	true, data }` or `{ ok: false, error }` and returns the same shape with a
122	`submittedAt: new Date().toISOString()` field added. Every return path inside `runAction`
123	passes through `stamp()`, including the early validation-failure return. The reason this
124	matters at all, rather than being pure overhead, is React's `useActionState` hook (the
125	client-side counterpart every form in src/components/domain/ built against a Server
126	Action uses): two consecutive submissions of the same form that both fail with an
127	identical error shape would otherwise be indistinguishable to a `useEffect` watching the
128	action's result for changes, since object identity is not guaranteed to differ and the
129	error payload could be byte-for-byte the same. A monotonically fresh `submittedAt` on every
130	single result — success or failure, validation or handler-thrown — guarantees the client
131	always has a new value to key off, even when everything else about two results is
132	identical.
133	
134	### DES-224 — Placeholder branded ids let create-time permission checks reuse the same `PermissionResource` shape
135	
136	- **Satisfies:** REQ-023
137	- **Decided in:** ADR-003, ADR-015
138	- **Code:** `src/actions/_lib/permission-resources.ts` — `PENDING_ISSUE_ID`, `PENDING_PROJECT_ID`, `PENDING_COMMENT_ID`, `PENDING_MEMBER_ID`
139	
140	`can()`'s `PermissionResource` type is a closed discriminated union (`src/types/permission.ts`),
141	and every resource variant — `{ kind: "issue", issueId, ... }`, `{ kind: "project",
142	projectId, ... }`, and so on — requires an id field even for an action like "may this actor
143	create an issue," where no issue exists yet to have an id. The file's own comment explains
144	the resolution: "asking 'may this actor create an issue in this project?' still has to name
145	an `issueId`. The ownership escalations inside `can()` compare ids for equality, and an
146	empty string never matches a real ULID — so a create check falls through to the role
147	matrix, which is exactly the intent." `PENDING_ISSUE_ID`, `PENDING_PROJECT_ID`,
148	`PENDING_COMMENT_ID` and `PENDING_MEMBER_ID` are each just `"" as <BrandedId>` — a value
149	that satisfies the type system's requirement for a branded id string without corresponding
150	to any row `insertIssue`, `insertProject`, `insertComment` or `insertMember` will ever
151	actually produce, since `newId()` (`src/lib/id.ts`) never generates an empty string. This
152	is a narrow, deliberate use of the branded-id escape hatch ADR-015 otherwise closes off
153	everywhere else in the codebase — the one place branded ids are cast from a raw literal
154	rather than produced by `newId()` or read back off a database row.
155	
156	### DES-225 — `ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID` and the deliberate layering exceptions this action layer accepts
157	
158	- **Satisfies:** REQ-208, REQ-211
159	- **Decided in:** ADR-001, ADR-013
160	- **Code:** `src/actions/_lib/permission-resources.ts` — `ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID`; `src/actions/profile/update-profile.ts`
161	
162	`ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID` is `"" as OrgId`, used exclusively as the first argument to
163	`consumeRateLimit()` inside `loginAction`, `requestPasswordResetAction` and
164	`confirmPasswordResetAction` — the three flows reachable before any session, hence any
165	`orgId`, exists. Because `consumeRateLimit`'s bucket key is `${orgId}:${bucketKey}`
166	(`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`), every unauthenticated caller sharing the same empty-string
167	`orgId` means the `auth:password-reset` and equivalent buckets are effectively global
168	rather than per-tenant for these three flows specifically — a deliberate trade documented
169	here rather than left implicit, since it is the one case in the whole rate-limiting design
170	where the bucket is not truly tenant-scoped.
171	
172	This document is also the right place to name, plainly, the layering exception the common
173	brief calls out as the most significant one in the action layer: `update-profile.ts` does
174	not call any service function at all. Its own comment states the reasoning: "the profile is
175	the one write with no service in front of it: there is no tenant rule, no event and no
176	quota to apply, so the action talks to `UserRepository` directly rather than inventing a
177	pass-through service." `updateProfileAction` still runs through `withAction` — it still
178	validates with `updateProfileSchema`, still resolves an `Actor` (with `requireOrg: false`,
179	per DES-221), still maps errors through `toActionResult` — but its handler calls
180	`updateUser` from `src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts` directly rather than through
181	a `UserService` that does not exist. Four other files in the corpus carry the same kind of
182	exception at the page-component level rather than the action level —
183	`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/profile/page.tsx`,
184	`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/members/invitations/page.tsx`,
185	`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/notifications/page.tsx`, and
186	`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/issues/[issueNumber]/page.tsx` — each
187	calling a repository function directly from a Server Component rather than through
188	src/server/services/. None of these five exceptions are accidents; they are documented in
189	the project's own commentary as intentional narrow bypasses of ADR-013's service-layer
190	boundary, made specifically for reads or writes with no permission rule, no event, and no
191	quota attached to them.
192	
193	## Invariants
194	
195	- `withAction`'s handler is never invoked before `schema.safeParse` has succeeded.
196	- Every `ActionResult` returned from `runAction` — success, validation failure, or
197	  handler-thrown error — carries a `submittedAt` stamp from the same call to `stamp()`.
198	- `resolveActorFor` never resolves an `Actor` for an organization the input did not name
199	  and the session's `activeOrgId` did not confirm.
200	- The four `PENDING_*` id constants are never equal to a real branded id produced by
201	  `newId()`.
202	- `update-profile.ts` is the only action file under src/actions/ that imports directly
203	  from src/server/repositories/ rather than from src/server/services/.
204	
205	## Test coverage
206	
207	`tests/lib/errors.test.ts` covers `toAppError`/`toActionResult`/`isDomainError` directly.
208	`tests/contract/permissions.test.ts` and `tests/server/permissions.test.ts` cover the
209	`can()` contract these action-layer checks call into, including the ownership-escalation
210	behavior `PENDING_*` ids are designed to fall through past. `tests/lib/rate-limit.test.ts`
211	covers `consumeRateLimit`'s bucket-key behavior, including the shared-bucket consequence of
212	`ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID`. There is no dedicated tests/actions/ directory in the corpus at all —
213	Server Action behavior is exercised indirectly through the service-layer tests
214	(`tests/services/*.test.ts`) that the actions' handlers ultimately delegate to, plus the
215	schema tests (`tests/schemas/*.test.ts`) that validate the Zod layer every `withAction` call
216	parses against before an actor is ever resolved.
217	
218	## Control flow: a validation failure versus a handler-thrown domain error
219	
220	```mermaid
221	flowchart TD
222	    A[raw input] --> B{schema.safeParse}
223	    B -- fail --> C[stamp(toActionResult(ZodError))]
224	    B -- success --> D[resolveActorFor]
225	    D -- no session/org --> E[throw UnauthorizedActionError]
226	    D -- resolved --> F[handler(parsed.data, actor)]
227	    F -- throws ForbiddenActionError/PlanLimitError/etc --> G[catch block]
228	    F -- throws service domain error --> G
229	    F -- resolves --> H[revalidateTagged(options.revalidate, profile)]
230	    E --> G
231	    G --> I[stamp(toActionResult(error))]
232	    H --> J[stamp({ ok: true, data })]
233	    C --> K[ActionResult returned to client]
234	    I --> K
235	    J --> K
236	```
237	
238	Both the early validation exit and every downstream throw converge on the same
239	`stamp(toActionResult(...))` call, which is precisely the "exactly one place" claim
240	`with-action.ts`'s header comment makes — there is no second, differently-shaped failure
241	path anywhere in the thirty-four actions built on this wrapper.

---
title: Server Action wrapper, errors and permission resources
id: DES-ACTION-CORE
status: approved
owners: [platform-team, d.okafor]
last_updated: 2026-06-12
related: [REQ-200, REQ-210, REQ-211, ADR-001, ADR-003, ADR-009, ADR-014, DES-070, DES-100]
---

## Purpose

This document covers the three files under src/actions/_lib/: `with-action.ts`,
`action-errors.ts` and `permission-resources.ts`. Every Server Action in the corpus except
five deliberately documented exceptions funnels through `withAction()`. These three files
are the load-bearing plumbing of the entire mutation surface — the four responsibilities
the common brief lists for every mutation ("validate, authenticate, translate errors,
revalidate") are implemented exactly once, here, rather than being re-implemented by each
of the thirty-nine action files.

`with-action.ts`'s own header comment states this concentration of responsibility
explicitly: "Owner D. Every mutation in `src/actions/**` funnels through here so the four
things each one must do — validate, authenticate, translate errors, revalidate — happen in
exactly one place." That sentence is the design thesis of the whole action layer, and this
document is where it gets unpacked function by function.

## Public surface

| function | signature | tables touched | pagination | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `withAction` | `<TSchema, TData>(schema, handler, options?) => (raw) => Promise<ActionResult<TData>>` | none directly | — | the wrapper itself |
| `resolveActorFor` (private) | `(input, fromInput) => Promise<Actor>` | none directly | — | orgSlug/orgId-from-input, else session |
| `stamp` (private) | `<T>(result) => ActionResult<T>` | none | — | attaches `submittedAt` |
| `UnauthorizedActionError` | class, `code: "unauthorized"` | — | — | no session, or session with no active org |
| `ForbiddenActionError` | class, `code: "forbidden"`, carries `action: PermissionAction` | — | — | `can()` returned false |
| `PlanLimitError` | class, `code: "plan_limit_exceeded"`, carries `resource`, `limit`, `used` | — | — | a `LimitedResource` quota would be breached |
| `RateLimitedError` | class, `code: "rate_limited"`, carries `bucketKey`, `resetAt` | — | — | `consumeRateLimit` refused |
| `FeatureUnavailableError` | class, `code: "forbidden"`, carries `flag` | — | — | a gating flag is off |
| `ActionNotFoundError` | class, `code: "not_found"`, carries `what` | — | — | row not found inside the actor's tenant |
| `PENDING_ISSUE_ID` / `PENDING_PROJECT_ID` / `PENDING_COMMENT_ID` / `PENDING_MEMBER_ID` | branded empty strings | — | — | create-time `can()` placeholders |
| `ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID` | branded empty string | — | — | rate-limit bucket owner pre-session |

### DES-220 — `withAction` is the single funnel for validate, authenticate, translate, revalidate

- **Satisfies:** REQ-200, REQ-211
- **Decided in:** ADR-001, ADR-009
- **Code:** `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts` — `withAction`

`withAction(schema, handler, options)` returns a closure — `runAction(raw)` — that a given
action file exports directly (or, more often, wraps in a one-line named export function so
the client-facing name matches the file, e.g. `archiveIssueAction`). Inside `runAction`,
the sequence is fixed: `schema.safeParse(raw)` first, returning a stamped failure
`ActionResult` immediately on a validation miss without ever calling the handler; then
`resolveActorFor()` to get an `Actor`; then the handler itself, wrapped in a `try/catch`
that routes every thrown error — domain errors from the service layer, the action-layer
error classes from `action-errors.ts`, or anything else — through `toActionResult()` (in
`src/lib/errors.ts`, described in the repository documents' cross-references as
ADR-014's error-code mapping). On success, `options.revalidate` tags are passed to
`revalidateTagged()` with `options.cacheProfile ?? CACHE_PROFILES.minutes` as the
cache-life profile Next 16 requires as `revalidateTag`'s second argument. This ordering —
validate before authenticate, authenticate before handle, handle before revalidate — is
uniform across all thirty-four actions that use `withAction`, which is what lets ADR-009's
shared-schema design (the same Zod schema validating both a client form and the action
input) actually hold: the schema is always the first gate, never bypassed by a handler that
might otherwise be tempted to read a raw field before validation completes.

### DES-221 — Actor resolution prefers the payload's own org identity over the session default

- **Satisfies:** REQ-210, REQ-211
- **Decided in:** ADR-001, ADR-006
- **Code:** `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts` — `resolveActorFor`, `ActionOptions.requireOrg`

`resolveActorFor(input, fromInput)` checks, when `fromInput` is true (the default, since
`ActionOptions.requireOrg` defaults to `true` when not explicitly set to `false`), whether
the already-Zod-parsed input object carries a non-empty `orgSlug` string or `orgId` string
field. If `orgSlug` is present it calls `getActor(orgSlug)`; if only `orgId` is present it
calls `requireActorFor(orgId as OrgId)`. Only when neither is present — or when
`options.requireOrg === false`, the path `updateProfileAction` uses — does it fall back to
`getSessionPrincipal()` and resolve against `principal.activeOrgId`, throwing
`UnauthorizedActionError` if there is no session or no active org. The doc comment on the
function explains the split in practical terms: "`getActor(orgSlug)` is the primary path
because most mutations are dispatched from a `[orgSlug]` route; actions whose payload
carries the branded `orgId` instead resolve through `requireActorFor()`." This preference
for the payload's own org identity over whatever happens to be the session's active org is
what makes it possible for a single browser session to have two tabs open on two different
organizations and mutate the correct one in each — the active-org fallback exists only for
the minority of actions, like `updateProfileAction`, that genuinely have no org-bearing
field in their payload to resolve against.

### DES-222 — Action-layer error classes mirror service-layer domain errors under one closed `ErrorCode` union

- **Satisfies:** REQ-138, REQ-193
- **Decided in:** ADR-014
- **Code:** `src/actions/_lib/action-errors.ts`

`action-errors.ts`'s header comment is explicit that these six classes exist at this layer
specifically: "these live in src/actions/_lib because only the action layer produces
them — services throw their own domain errors, and repositories throw none." Each class
carries a `readonly code` matching one of the nine `ErrorCode` values `HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE`
in `src/lib/errors.ts` maps to an HTTP status: `UnauthorizedActionError` →
`"unauthorized"` (401), `ForbiddenActionError` → `"forbidden"` (403, also shared with
`FeatureUnavailableError`), `PlanLimitError` → `"plan_limit_exceeded"` (402),
`RateLimitedError` → `"rate_limited"` (429), `ActionNotFoundError` → `"not_found"` (404).
This mirrors, rather than duplicates, the convention `PermissionDeniedError` and
`TenantScopeError` already establish at the service layer — both layers independently throw
typed errors that `toAppError()` translates by `instanceof` check, and `isDomainError()` in
`src/lib/errors.ts` recognizes the service-layer set but not this action-layer set by name,
because `toActionResult`'s catch-all branch (returning `{ code: "internal_error", ... }`)
is only reached for errors *neither* layer recognizes — the action-layer classes are
recognized through their own `readonly code` field being read directly in some call sites
and through structural equivalence with the service-layer mapping pattern in others. The
practical effect for a form author: whichever layer detects the problem first, the shape of
what reaches the browser is identical.

### DES-223 — `stamp()` attaches `submittedAt` so `useActionState` can distinguish two results

- **Satisfies:** REQ-200
- **Decided in:** ADR-001
- **Code:** `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts` — `stamp`

`stamp<T>(result)` is a tiny function — it takes an `ActionResult<T>` that is either `{ ok:

### DES-224 — Placeholder branded ids let create-time permission checks reuse the same `PermissionResource` shape

- **Satisfies:** REQ-023
- **Decided in:** ADR-003, ADR-015

`can()`'s `PermissionResource` type is a closed discriminated union (`src/types/permission.ts`),

### DES-225 — `ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID` and the deliberate layering exceptions this action layer accepts

- **Satisfies:** REQ-208, REQ-211
- **Decided in:** ADR-001, ADR-013
- **Code:** `src/actions/_lib/permission-resources.ts` — `ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID`; `src/actions/profile/update-profile.ts`

`ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID` is `"" as OrgId`, used exclusively as the first argument to

This document is also the right place to name, plainly, the layering exception the common

`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/profile/page.tsx`,
`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/members/invitations/page.tsx`,

## Test coverage

`tests/lib/errors.test.ts` covers `toAppError`/`toActionResult`/`isDomainError` directly.

flowchart TD

    B -- fail --> C[stamp(toActionResult(ZodError))]
    B -- success --> D[resolveActorFor]
    D -- no session/org --> E[throw UnauthorizedActionError]
    D -- resolved --> F[handler(parsed.data, actor)]
    F -- throws ForbiddenActionError/PlanLimitError/etc --> G[catch block]
    F -- throws service domain error --> G
    F -- resolves --> H[revalidateTagged(options.revalidate, profile)]
    E --> G
    G --> I[stamp(toActionResult(error))]
    H --> J[stamp({ ok: true, data })]

    J --> K

content.text:
## Findings

I checked the plan-quota table, the feature-flag percentage-rollout strategy, the rate-limiter bucket config, and the error-code mapping against the code that implements each, and found contradictions in four places:

**1. Plan quotas** — `docs/requirements/billing-and-plan-limits.md` (REQ-134) states "3 projects on free, 10 on starter, 100 on growth." The actual table in `src/config/plan-limits.ts` has `free.projects = 2` (3 is the free `seats` value, not `projects`). Every other document that restates the ladder (ADR-010, the 2026-02-10 pricing notes, the table in `docs/api/actions-billing.md`) gets it right as 2 — only this one requirement transposes the numbers.

**2. Percentage rollout** — `docs/requirements/feature-flags.md` (REQ-189) asserts the `ai_issue_summary` percentage strategy "hashes the organization's id (**not** the acting user's)" and that "the rollout decision does not depend on the acting user, only the organization." The actual `bucketOf()` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` hashes `` `${flag}:${ctx.orgId}:${ctx.userId}` `` — the user id is part of the seed, so two members of the same org can land in different buckets, contradicting the "every member sees the same on/off state" claim.

**3. Refill-rate / rate-limiter keying** — `docs/adr/ADR-011-in-process-rate-limiter.md` and `docs/ops/notes-2026-01-30-rate-limiter-sizing.md` both state that `auth:password-reset` "is charged per identity (email address attempted) rather than per organization." In the actual code (`src/server/services/auth-service.ts`, `src/actions/auth/reset-password.ts`), every anonymous call passes a fixed sentinel `ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID`/`ANONYMOUS_ORG` constant — the bucket is one shared global counter, not scoped per email at all.

**4. Error codes an action can actually return** — `docs/design/action-wrapper-and-errors.md` (DES-222) claims the action-layer error classes (`PlanLimitError`, `RateLimitedError`, `ForbiddenActionError`, etc.) "are recognized through their own `readonly code` field being read directly ... or through structural equivalence."
